name: Upstash
tagline: Serverless Redis, QStash, Vector, Workflow, and REST APIs.
shortDescription: Upstash exposes Redis REST, QStash messaging, Vector, Workflow, Kafka, and a CLI built for agents and automation.
agentSummary: Agents can provision lightweight state, queues, vector indexes, and scheduled workflows with HTTP-first APIs.
bestFor: Serverless Redis, queues, rate limiting, vector search, workflows, and cron-like jobs.
cautionNotes: Key limitations: Queue fanout, deletes, and token exposure need careful scoping. Schema changes, migrations, deletes, backups, row-level security, and retention policies need explicit review before agents touch production data. CLI access is powerful but can run destructive local or production commands; prefer dry runs, preview environments, and non-production credentials. API automation needs client-side throttling, idempotency where supported, pagination limits, retries, and audit logging.
pricingSummary: Public usage-based pricing with free tiers across products.
authModel: REST URLs/tokens, API keys, and environment variables.
browserSupport: Console supports database, token, usage, and log inspection.

capabilities.detail: CLI can run Redis commands against the REST API and manage resources.
Redis REST, QStash, Vector, and management APIs are documented.
Official docs are listed for API behavior, authentication, limits, examples, and setup review.
Pricing is public across Redis, QStash, Vector, and Workflow.
Console supports database, token, usage, and log inspection.
The tool has documented test, local, preview, self-hosted, or staging paths that let agents validate changes away from production.
